runners_data.name: Kodi Fire
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 70 with a recent 1m Good-ground win and trainer Charles Hills in 1-from-14 form over 14 days; genuine hold-up style that suits a sprint finish, and the blinkers (hg:t) sharpen focus — course-distance profile is the standout in this field.

runners_data.name: Darvel
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old returning quickly (7 days) after a 13th at this trip on Good, and while Patrick Chamings has a runner in form, its true hold-up inclination means it was remapped to midfield for this six-runner field — style fitness tagged at 0.93 tempers confidence it can reproduce its best.

runners_data.name: Pentonville
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at 3 years old with a recent win (1st/8f/STA) and placed effort at 1m2f Good, Henry Callan's mount has shown enough positional versatility to be the most credible forward-going force here; 5 days since last run is not a concern given the recent run of form.

runners_data.name: Palazzo Persico
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Soft last time and has struggled at 8f on Standard/All-Weather, making this trip and surface switch relevant; its natural rear-ranging style is compressed into midfield here given the queue of hold-up horses, reducing its ability to deliver from its optimal deep position.

runners_data.name: Endowed
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning from a 263-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — after wins at 6f on Good going; stepping up dramatically in trip to 8f asks questions that the layoff only compounds, and though remapped to midfield, its genuine style is as a closer over shorter, diminishing its chance.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: Miss Evie Lee (7lb claimer) partnering the lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 51) off a 10-day break; recent form includes a U (unseated) and an 8th, and a tongue-tie and visor combination suggests a horse that needs managing — its style fit score of 0.90 is the weakest in the race, and recent Going form (2 from 15 on similar ground) is uninspiring.

races.paceDynamic: Brighton's undulating mile with its long run-in presents a field where every single runner is a natural hold-up type, meaning no horse has a genuine inclination to lead — the pace will almost certainly be pedestrian early before the field concertinas and a sprint develops from the home turn. With Kodi Fire, Darvel, Pentonville, Palazzo Persico, Endowed, and Wrist Art all preferring to race in rear, the early gallop will be set by whoever is pushed forward out of necessity rather than inclination, likely crawling into the false straight before a mass surge in the final two furlongs. This race shape heavily favours the horse with the best finishing kick from a clean position — specifically those whose hold-up style is genuine and whose amateur jockey can balance them into the sprint, rather than those shuffled back by traffic. Pentonville is the most naturally prominent runner of the bunch based on recent positional history and thus best placed to dictate from a comfortable stalking berth; the field holds more hold-up types than can all sit last, meaning Palazzo Persico, Endowed, and Wrist Art are most likely to be squeezed into midfield against their will and least likely to secure their natural deep position.

watchPoints.text: Pentonville is the only runner with a credible recent positional record close to the pace — watch whether Henry Callan elects to go forward from the gate, which would transform the race shape entirely.

Kodi Fire's form is the strongest at this trip and going combination but Mr James Hills (7) is an amateur claiming rider — watch for any position-management issues from the rear in a pedestrian-paced race where late movers may get boxed in.

Endowed returns from 263 days off and Miss Imogen Mathias (5lb claimer) is aboard — any signs of rustiness or greenness early could leave it detached from the sprint that develops, making its chance near-negligible.

With all six runners preferring to race held up, watch the first two furlongs closely — whichever horse is pushed forward involuntarily will set the tone, and if that horse is Palazzo Persico or Wrist Art (lowest ORs), the pace will be too slow to suit genuine closers.
Darvel runs back quickly after just 7 days — trainer Patrick Chamings has 1 win from 7 in the 14-day window, so watch the market move rather than assuming fitness is confirmed.

runners_data.name: Amber Honey

runners_data.name: Night Bear
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old confirmed front runner who has finished in the first four six times from fifteen starts on Good ground; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he is listed as prominent rather than a pure leader, but the pace notes confirm he leads — his ability to control from the front is the race's defining factor.

runners_data.name: Power Of Prayer
runners_data.note: Holds a recent win over 12f on Standard and two thirds at 10f on Good, suggesting course-relevant stamina; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a meaningful weight advantage in a low-OR handicap and he profiles as the strongest candidate to attack Night Bear late.

runners_data.name: Koko Blue
runners_data.note: Finished third over 12f on Good on his most comparable outing but carries a ⚠ fade flag and has been absent 45 days — Tom Clover's 2-from-12 14-day record is modest, and this horse needs a strong pace it is unlikely to get here to prevent his typical late weakening.

runners_data.name: Sarangpur
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield zone by redistribution; the ⚠ fade flag and limited Good-ground form (2 runs) compound the challenge of racing out of natural position, and the false pace created by Night Bear's solo lead works against him.

runners_data.name: Suitcase Smith
runners_data.note: True closer shuffled into the midfield map position because the rear is over-subscribed; John Berry has gone 0-from-6 over the past 14 days and this horse's best Good-ground finish was a fourth at 10f — needs cover and a searching pace neither of which is likely here.

runners_data.name: La Trinite
runners_data.note: Returns from a 333-day absence for Neil King, who has no runners flagged over the past 14 days; held up naturally but forced into midfield on the map, and the combination of extreme layoff and positional compromise makes meaningful participation hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Douglas Dc
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has found the frame four times in fifteen Good-ground starts, suggesting reliable if modest form — true hold-up type wearing blinkers, redirected to midfield on the map, but his 16f placed form hints at the stamina to stay if the race develops slowly enough.

runners_data.name: Gearing's Point
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and posts the most consistent placed recent record in this field (5,2,5,3 in last four at 12f), all on Good or Standard; a natural closer who has been mapped to midfield through redistribution, and his track record at this trip on this going makes him the most credible beneficiary if the closers do land a blow.

races.paceDynamic: Night Bear is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, he should slot into an uncontested lead and control a steady, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f Brighton trip on Good ground. The rest of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Suitcase Smith, Sarangpur, La Trinite, Douglas Dc and Gearing's Point are all true closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear cannot absorb all of them, and their natural positions will be compressed behind Night Bear. With a single pace-setter setting a measured tempo and the closing ranks bunched together, there is every chance the pace is insufficient to string the field out, leaving a cluttered finish where those able to travel closer to the pace from the outset — Power Of Prayer, Amber Honey and Koko Blue — are best positioned to pounce. This race shape clearly favours horses with genuine hold-up ability who can still track the pace from a handy position, rather than deep closers who need a truly searching gallop to generate the late momentum that will not materialise here.

watchPoints.text: Night Bear — if he is allowed to bowl along unopposed and the tempo is genuinely slow, his front-running package could prove very difficult to reel in; monitor whether any rider attempts to challenge him early, as no challenge means he names his own price.

Gearing's Point — the most in-form closer in the race on Good ground over 12f, but Dougie Costello must find a clear passage from a compressed midfield pack; a traffic problem exiting the final bend would cost him any realistic chance.

Power Of Prayer — Jack Callan's 3lb claim lightens the load meaningfully at OR=53, but the horse's last three runs at 16f, 12f and 12f on Standard suggest he may need a searching pace to see out 1m4f on Good; watch for signs of tiring in the final 2f.

La Trinite — 333 days off the track is an extreme layoff for any horse, and Neil King's 0-from-0 14-day record means there is no recent stable form to anchor confidence; treat as a non-runner for analytical purposes unless market support signals otherwise.

Sarangpur — 49-day absence combined with the ⚠ fade flag and the softer-ground bias in his recent form (four of last five on Soft or Heavy) raises a genuine concern about whether Good ground here is far enough on the fast side to suit him today.

runners_data.name: West Hill Rosie

runners_data.name: Masqool
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll runner with headgear (tongue-tie/visor flagged) who is a genuine hold-up horse at heart — although shown in midfield on the pace map due to the volume of rear-runners in this field, he will likely be searching for cover rather than being prominent, and his 0W1P from 15 similar-going runs underlines the stiff task.

runners_data.name: Twilight Guest
runners_data.note: Consistent course and distance profile (2W4P from 11 runs on Good) and fitted with a hood, but this 6yo's natural style is to come from behind — he ends up mapped to midfield purely because the field is stacked with hold-up types, and the lack of a strong pace is a genuine tactical obstacle to him producing his best.

runners_data.name: Dogged
runners_data.note: A 9yo veteran fitted with a hood whose recent form reads 5-8-0-9-9, struggling to land a blow on Good ground over 12f; genuinely stays at the rear and, without a strong pace to chase, has little prospect of getting involved from his natural position.

runners_data.name: Lucky Sevens
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides for in-form James Owen (11/58 last 14 days) and this 3yo has a progressive profile — a win on Good over 8f and a placed effort on similar going — making her the most interesting of the hold-up group if she can find a position to pounce from; the switch to 1m2f is a query but breeding and recent form suggest she stays.

races.paceDynamic: Rockafeller Skank is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, will control the tempo from the outset on Good ground at Brighton's undulating 1m2f. With a four-race winning streak and a consistent front-running record over this sort of trip and going, she shapes to set a measured, sustainable pace that punishes horses who lack a finishing gear. The remainder of the field — Masqool, Twilight Guest, Dogged, West Hill Rosie, and Lucky Sevens — are all natural hold-up types, meaning no rival is likely to apply genuine pressure early and force an honest gallop. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can lead and control from the front, or a prominent racer with enough class to latch onto the leader's coat-tails and quicken from there; true hold-up horses will need a strong pace they are unlikely to get. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Masqool, Twilight Guest, and Dogged are the most likely to push forward out of character to try to improve their positions.

watchPoints.text: Rockafeller Skank — watch the break: if she gets away cleanly and opens up a lead of two or more lengths by the 1m mark, the race is likely already over given the total absence of any rival willing to press her.
Lucky Sevens — watch where Billy Loughnane positions her in the early stages; if she tracks Rockafeller Skank within two lengths, she becomes a live threat to pick up the pieces in the final furlong.

Masqool, Twilight Guest, Dogged — watch to see if any of the three hold-up types break their natural pattern and push forward to try to find a prominent position; if they do, the pace shape changes materially and the race opens up.

West Hill Rosie — watch the final two furlongs specifically; her flagged tendency to fade means she may look competitive at the top of the straight before weakening, which could mislead in-running readings.

Rockafeller Skank's freshness — she runs just three days after her last victory; watch her pre-race demeanour and early racing behaviour for any sign she is too keen or over-fresh, which could cause her to burn her petrol prematurely.

runners_data.name: Gretna Dreams
runners_data.note: The four-year-old has shown she can win on good ground (two wins on good) and over this trip, but the overcrowded closer's berth means she'll be shuffled into a mid-pack role that doesn't suit her best; Stuart Williams has drawn a blank in 14 days and the 0.92 style-fit flag tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Man Is King
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon partners this seven-year-old who has a strong record at this level — two wins from five on good ground and a recent winning run — and his prominent style makes him the most natural foil to The Wicked Wolf; headgear (t) has been worn before and the 6-day turnaround is tight but he clearly comes here in form.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old is the hold-up horse best suited to adapting, with a recent course win at a sprint trip and consistent placed efforts; the 10/45 trainer 14-day strike rate is a minor positive, the blinkers are a known factor, and though he'll likely be asked to race a touch forward of his ideal spot, he has the class to make it work.

runners_data.name: The Wicked Wolf
runners_data.note: A 255-day absence is the single biggest flag here — last ran in October and has only three runs to her name — but she is the confirmed lone front-runner and her form includes a win on soft; the 0.93 style-fit tag reflects that her mapped prominent role is where she'll actually race, not a repositioning, so the flag relates to the front-running load rather than being out of role.

runners_data.name: Extraterrestrial
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's three-year-old has been placed on good ground and stays the trip adequately, though the 13/10f good outing (13th) on similar terms is a concern; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is useful, and with only 2/8 on similar going the evidence for a big run is thin.

runners_data.name: Meritocratic
runners_data.note: A three-year-old hold-up type fitted with a visor, stepping back onto good ground after a run on soft where she showed a little improvement; the trainer has a blank 14-day record and only 2/5 on similar going, so she needs to improve on her form profile to threaten.

runners_data.name: Virtue Chastity
runners_data.note: Returning from a 127-day break, which is a significant fitness question mark, and at three years old she is the youngest and least exposed runner in the field; Jack Dace's 5lb claim helps the weight, but her hold-up style will be further compromised by the crowded rear, and there is simply not enough evidence on good ground to be confident.

races.paceDynamic: The Wicked Wolf is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap over Brighton's undulating 1m2f, and with no credible rival likely to press hard for the lead from the outset, she can dictate terms at a measured, controllable gallop under Saffie Osborne. Man Is King is the only genuine prominent racer likely to sit close to the pace, meaning the early tempo is unlikely to be severe and the leader may steal a decisive advantage on the descent. The field is unusually loaded with hold-up horses — Lenny's Spirit, Gretna Dreams, Danehill Star and Virtue Chastity are all natural closers, but the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear, and several will be forced to race in a more prominent mid-pack berth than their true style demands; of these, Danehill Star and Gretna Dreams are best placed to slot into a workable position. A single honest pace-setter on good ground at Brighton, where the track naturally rewards those who travel prominently into the final hill, creates a race shape that strongly favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles.

watchPoints.text: The Wicked Wolf's 255-day absence is the single most consequential unknown in the race — if she shows any signs of rustiness in the early stages or fails to stride out fluently past the two-furlong dip, the entire race shape collapses and the value in the prominent/front-running scenarios evaporates immediately.

Man Is King has run six days ago and reappears quickly — watch to see if he travels with his usual zest in the early stages, because if he is slightly flat he may not apply the expected pressure and the race becomes a procession for The Wicked Wolf.

With Lenny's Spirit, Gretna Dreams, Danehill Star and Virtue Chastity all natural hold-up types, the back straight is likely to be congested — watch the post-race sectionals and in-running position reports, as any horse caught in a pocket turning for home at Brighton has almost no room to recover on this narrow track.

Danehill Star is worth monitoring in the pre-race market: Tony Carroll's 10/45 recent trainer form and the horse's ability to adapt his style mean any market move could signal stable confidence in him outrunning the race shape.

Brighton's good ground has been consistent across all seven races on today's card — no horse should face a going surprise, but watch for any reported post-inspection changes that could soften conditions and reduce the advantage of the front-runner.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Sandman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 7f Brighton contest and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push him from the outset, he can dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo on good ground. The field is overwhelmingly hold-up in style, meaning the majority of runners will be racing behind him with little to disrupt his rhythm through the sweeping Brighton bends. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a sustainable pace — classically compresses the finish into a stamina-test finale on the uphill run-in rather than a sprint, rewarding horses who can travel well and produce a sustained effort rather than a devastating late burst. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Fai Fai, Embarked, Mokata, My Boy Jack, My Mate Beattie, She Went Whoosh, Almavillalobas and Imthequeenofsheba all compete for limited space in the back half of the field, and many will unavoidably race closer than their natural style. This race shape most favours horses with prominent or tracking credentials who can latch onto the sole pace-setter and produce a sustained challenge from two furlongs out — Barnsnape Boy, Shes Got The Blues and Spirited Dancer profile best under this configuration.

watchPoints.text: Mister Sandman's ability to secure and hold the lead unchallenged is the pivotal factor — if anything rushes him in the opening furlong, the entire pace architecture shifts and hold-up horses gain ground they would not otherwise make.

The sheer density of hold-up runners — Embarked, My Boy Jack, Almavillalobas, My Mate Beattie, She Went Whoosh, Imthequeenofsheba and Mokata all competing for the same rear-field positions — creates a high risk of traffic problems and interference from two furlongs out on the narrow Brighton straight.

Shes Got The Blues is the most credible hold-up horse on form credentials and going data, but Billy Loughnane will need to find a route through the compressed midfield cluster early in the straight; watch her position as they straighten.

Barnsnape Boy's recent 7f-good win on 12 days' rest is the most relevant piece of form in the race — note whether Murphy (7) settles him just off Mister Sandman's shoulder, as that is the optimum tactical position given the race shape.

Fai Fai is declared a NON-RUNNER — bettors and analysts relying on early pace maps that include this horse should recalibrate, as the field is now entirely minus a horse that had genuine positional ambiguity near the front.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a recent win over 5f on Good ground in this sim-going category (1W4P); apprentice Liam Wright claims 5lb, which is meaningful in a low-weight field, and the step back to 5½f at Brighton suits his late-running profile if Hoodie Hoo sets a genuine pace.

runners_data.name: Hoodie Hoo
runners_data.note: Charles Hills has form at 1/14 runners over the last 14 days and this horse carries tongue strap; the confirmed pace-setter here, though its STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects a horse that may be racing slightly out of its most effective role, and 44 days off is worth monitoring for freshness effects.

runners_data.name: The Thames Boatman
runners_data.note: Gelding with progressive Brighton form including a recent win on Good and a place on Firm — course specialist with strong recent sim-going figures (1W1P); prominent racer who could push Hoodie Hoo for the lead early, and headgear (p) suggests he races handily and with focus under Finley Marsh.

runners_data.name: Rogue Bullet
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent type with two wins over this trip on Good and Standard in recent history, but Billy Loughnane is riding this horse back after a 53-day absence and its natural front-running style is compromised by displacement to midfield; the STYLE_FIT discount applies and it will need a pace collapse to hit the frame.

runners_data.name: The Flying Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old holds a Going form query with just 1W3P on similar conditions but has been placed four times on Good recently; Mason Paetel claims 5lb, providing a weight advantage, though the hood (b) and inconsistent form string (5-4640) makes it hard to trust at the sharp end without a specific pace trigger.

runners_data.name: Correspondence
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's hold-up runner arrives 26 days fresh with strong recent form (826312) including a win on Good and multiple placed efforts; it's a true closer in nature but repositioned to midfield because of field congestion at the rear — the 7lb claim from Myla Coppins helps, but it needs things to go right tactically to get involved.

races.paceDynamic: Hoodie Hoo is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field over 5½f at Brighton, sets up a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front without any rival likely to match strides aggressively. The Thames Boatman will attempt to race prominently and may press from early, but with Rogue Bullet and Correspondence displaced from their natural prominent and hold-up slots respectively, the race shape is more structured than the redistribution suggests. This field holds more genuine front-running and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate — Rogue Bullet and Correspondence are true prominent/hold-up horses who are unlikely to fully express their natural style here, with Hoodie Hoo and The Thames Boatman best placed to control the tempo. A single, unhurried front-runner at Brighton's undulating 5½f course sets up favourably for hold-up horses who can travel through the race and produce a late run, making genuine closers and horses who settle well behind the pace the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Moulin Booj — if Hoodie Hoo gets a clear lead and the pace is sustainable, Liam Wright's 5lb claim gives him real momentum late over 5½f on Good ground and he arrives on the back of a recent sim-going win.

The Thames Boatman — watch whether Finley Marsh elects to press Hoodie Hoo from the break; if The Thames Boatman quickens into second early, it turns Scenario B live and significantly changes the pace shape.

Rogue Bullet — 53 days off is a notable absence for a horse being mapped out of its natural role; if it comes on strong from a handy position it may signal the pace is slow enough to negate the redistribution entirely.

Correspondence — monitor its draw and early foot; if Myla Coppins can slot it into a genuine tracking position rather than being forced wide, the horse's recent form makes it a dangerous outsider despite its style-fit discount.

The Flying Seagull — the blinkers are a headgear flag worth watching in running; if it travels well in midfield and the front pair tire, Mason Paetel's 5lb claim could make it competitive at a price despite its inconsistent recent record.
